reviewMethod: Assistant visual screening using local OpenCV with cv2.setNumThreads(1): 24 timestamped RGB frames per clip evenly sampled from 0.1s to duration-0.1s; each full contact sheet actually inspected via view_image. Four clips (73, 76, 79, 100) additionally inspected as 32 evenly spaced source frames retained during sequential decoding. Sequential decoding is not continuous visual review. No dataset-provided code executed. Selection: 24 rounded equally spaced indices across 59 numerically ID-sorted eligible, previously unreviewed publisher-positive clips in requested 71-140 range (selected endpoints 73 and 140).
limitations: Provisional assistant annotations from sampled still images, not human ground truth, continuous playback or frame-by-frame visual inspection. No labels approved solely from publisher categories.
Temporal spans approximate sampled contact configurations; exact onset/offset, continuity, actual impacts and force remain unverified. Unannotated margins are unknown, not normal.

Only full four-second windows are eligible: positive coverage must be at least 50%; normal coverage must explicitly cover the entire window. This review approves no normal intervals. Short/unclear contact is left ambiguous.
Visible stick-like props trigger whole-recording exclusion for this unarmed physical-fight target. No inference about identity, intent, injury or crime.

All VID footage belongs to one training cohort. Actor/session lineage is unknown; descriptive sceneGroup values do not establish independent actors or sessions. No calibration/holdout independence claim.
Consent is author-reported and not an independently verified full release; rights evidence remains in DATA-RIGHTS.md and vid-source.json.
One initial supplemental source frame for v_c_b_76 is black. Primary 24-frame sheet is visible; the black image supports no label.

recordings.notes: Three people; sampled arm/upper-body contact and bending around 1.8-3.4s, followed by separation/repositioning and a late short contact episode. Supplemental 32-frame sheet does not support a conservative two-second contact span without including uncertain transitions. No normal full window approved.

Supplemental 32-frame sheet still shows intermittent rather than a clearly supported two-second contact span. One supplemental first frame is black; no label is inferred from it. No normal full window approved.

Three people with repeated arm extensions and brief apparent hand/shoulder contact. The supplemental 32-frame sheet does not resolve directed contact versus gesturing/positioning sufficiently to retain a positive interval. No normal full window approved.
